name: SETAR Colocation Datacenter
notes: Official SETAR page describes its colocation datacenter with dual high-capacity feeds, redundant UPS and backup generators; capacity not disclosed.

name: Recommended Caribbean Netherlands main government data center
developer: Government of the Caribbean Netherlands / central government study
notes: Report says Bonaire has a modernized government data facility but recommends placing the main future government data center on Bonaire; not yet evidence of approval or construction.

name: Candidate secondary Caribbean Netherlands government data center
developer: Government of the Caribbean Netherlands / central government study
notes: Report says Saba currently has only small server rooms and recommends a second facility on either Saba or Sint Eustatius; candidate location only.

name: Candidate secondary Caribbean Netherlands government data center
developer: Government of the Caribbean Netherlands / central government study
notes: Report says Sint Eustatius currently has only small server rooms and recommends a second facility on either Sint Eustatius or Saba; candidate location only.

name: Blue NAP Americas
notes: Official site offers colocation, private cloud and managed datacenter services in Curacao; Data Center Map lists the Willemstad site at Seru Mahuma with 5 MW; AMS-IX announced a POP in the BNA data centre in 2019.

name: CORE Datacenter
notes: Registry page lists CORE N.V.'s Tier III-certified datacenter at 18 Vesuviusstraat, Willemstad with redundant power/cooling and 24/7 NOC; capacity not disclosed.

name: E-Commerce Park N.V. data center
notes: Data Center Map lists E-Commerce Park in Willemstad as a Caribbean colocation/disaster-recovery data center with submarine cable access; capacity not disclosed.

name: Kolo NL2 Meppel
notes: Official Kolo page describes NL2 Meppel at Ketelskamp 10 as a high-efficiency colocation data center serving Northern Netherlands; capacity not disclosed on official page.

name: Cellnex Hoogersmilde datacenter
notes: Official Cellnex page lists Hoogersmilde with 350 m2 total surface and 860 kVA total capacity; converted here as 0.86 MW nominal apparent power.

name: Kolo NL1 Dronten / Serverius SDC1
notes: Kolo official site lists NL1 Dronten among Netherlands data centers; Data Center Platform lists Serverius SDC1 Dronten at De Linge 26 with 200-500 racks.

name: Cellnex Lelystad datacenter
notes: Official Cellnex page lists Lelystad with 180 m2 total surface and 450 kVA total capacity, realized in the tower in March 2018.

name: Meta Zeewolde hyperscale data center
notes: DCD reported Meta behind a proposed 166-hectare Trekkersveld IV campus; NL Times reported the Council of State struck down the zoning plan after Meta withdrew, meaning the project could not be revived under that plan.

name: Penta Infra LEE01
notes: Official Penta Infra page lists LEE01 in Leeuwarden with 450 kW IT capacity, 400 m2 IT space and Tier III+ equivalent compliance.

name: Penta Infra LEE02
notes: Official Penta Infra page lists LEE02 in Leeuwarden with 400 kW IT capacity, 400 m2 IT space and Tier III+ equivalent compliance.

name: Cellnex Tjerkgaast / Spannenburg datacenter
notes: Official Cellnex page lists Tjerkgaast / Spannenburg with 50 m2 total surface and 225 kVA total capacity; it notes the tower datacenter opened in partnership with ViaData in 2016.

name: InterDC Doetinchem
notes: Official InterDC page says it acquired the Doetinchem datacenter in 2021; site is Tier 3-designed, ISO27001/NEN7510 certified, has 120 racks and possible second-room expansion.

name: Cellnex Ugchelen datacenter
notes: Official Cellnex page lists Ugchelen with 75 m2 total surface and 150 kVA total capacity; page states the tower was bought in 2007 to house a datacenter.

name: Google Eemshaven data center
notes: Official Google data center page says Google announced a EUR600 million Eemshaven data centre in 2014 and opened the first Dutch data centre there in December 2016.

name: NorthC Groningen 1 & 2
notes: Official NorthC page describes two data centers at Groningen's Westpoort business park; Groningen 2 uses green-hydrogen fuel-cell emergency generators.

name: QTS Groningen data center
notes: Official QTS page describes its Groningen data center as one of the largest in the Northern Netherlands and located within the FLAP market area.
